utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. Please be seated. May we hear the case number by Madam Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian, Ann Sutherland, and Ruth Karper for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask, before we start with today's witness, is there anything to be discussed beforehand? A number of deadlines are set for today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's why Mr. Ostojic will not be in the courtroom with us today. He is trying with the case manager to meet all the deadlines, and we hope that we will fulfill all the Chamber's requirements for today. Also, I would like to state that we withdraw Witness 055 and Witness 083 from the list of the witnesses. Those witnesses are scheduled for this week. And during the day, we'll ask the Chamber to approve two new witnesses which would probably --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Let me start step by step.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. Thank you for the hint. Witness 055, Witness 083, you mentioned scheduled for this week, this would mean that Defence has no witnesses this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Defence has Witness 006 and 043.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So this is -- may be misleading on the transcript. Therefore, my question on line 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to answer something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No, because it should only be transpired from the transcript that you did not withdraw a witness scheduled for this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, not all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. So this is the final decision related to these two witnesses. What about the I would say already famous 058, trying already twice?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This witness is scheduled for the last week, so I have to admit that we didn't contact him yesterday. And we can instruct our investigator to contact him, but not during this day because he is already overburdened with the task we gave him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think in the moment, we are all overburdened with the tasks. And I really can understand your point. Additional remarks from your side?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the day, we'll submit the list of the witnesses for the next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. What about Prosecution, anything special for today?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We do have the English-language copy of the constitution to distribute today, but are still looking for a B/C/S copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And please, let's try to settle as soon as possible the problem with the different copies of the statute. Then before the witness arrived related to the admonition in this concrete case, a special question to the Prosecution, in another context, we discussed this previously. I have to admonish this witness under Rule 90, no doubt. This would mean that the Chamber has under the rules or seem to have the power to compel a witness to answer a question which might tend to incriminate the witness. I think as to the fact that this person, in fact, appears as a witness but let's call it, it's a borderline case to being an accused, and this Tribunal doesn't have the power to stop any, say, national court to make use of the statements given in this Tribunal. I think the general principle applies that a person cannot be compelled to give any kind of self-incriminatory testimony. Do you accept this, or do you have a different view?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I do have a slightly different view. If Your Honour prefers, I'd rather wait and see if this theoretical question actually arises. I'm not sure the witness is going to invoke any right against self-incrimination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Then may I ask the usher, please, to escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just on that point, Your Honour, at that point, I would ask that we go into closed session if that arises, and then we can address the issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think the admonition has to be in open session. And as for the moment, I have no request by the witness to start in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't have such a request, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Budimir. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You are called as a witness of the Chamber. And therefore, opposed to a witness called by any party, we didn't have any possibility of contacting you beforehand. So therefore, my first question, from your point of view, do you have reasons that your testimony is taken not in public session or under certain to-be-defined protective measures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then it is my duty to give you a general information on your rights. In this Tribunal, as it is true in all the courtrooms of the world, a witness is expected to tell the truth and nothing but the truth, and the entire truth. This means also an omission to tell something one would expect you to testify in a concrete context could be seen as a false testimony. On the other hand, we have to act based on that what we have in evidence until now. And as to the fact that this is already Day 126 of the case, you will believe that we have heard a lot, and we maybe know already a lot. But until the end of the case, we have to listen carefully and to try to come closer to the truth. This means we are, to a certain end, dependent on the truthfulness of your testimony. On the other hand, there's a general principle of nonself-incrimination. In our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, Rule 90, paragraph (E), it reads: "The witness may object to making any statement which might tend to incriminate the witness. The Chamber, may however, compel the witness to answer the question. Testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against the witness for any offence other than false testimony." To be quite clear, you are here not as an accused but as a witness. But it might be that there are such questions, and in this case, the Trial Chamber takes a slightly different approach one could summarise as follows: Any witness may refuse to answer any questions, the reply to which would subject him or one of the relatives to the risk of being prosecuted for a criminal offence. And it's my duty to inform you on your right to refuse those answers. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. On the other hand, in addition, once again, due to the fact that prior to reaching this courtroom, none of the parties had had the possibility to give you the advice and the admonition under Rule 91. Before we start, and not for a concrete reason based on your testimony, I have to advise you that any false testimony under solemn declaration in this Tribunal is punishable, and the maximum penalty for false testimony under solemn declaration shall be a fine of 100.000 Euros or a term of imprisonment or seven years or both. Did you understand this information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understood everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then it's time to take your solemn declaration. Would you please stand up and give us your solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then let us start immediately with your personal data. May we hear your name, your first names, if more than one, and in case there is such a nickname, also your nickname.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: My name is Slavko Budimir, last name is Budimir. And my nickname is Budo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And your father's and mother's name, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: My father's name is Rade and my mother's name is Bosiljka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And you were born when and where?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I was born on the 20th of August 1953 in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You are married, and do you have a child or children?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, I am married. My wife's name is Gordana, and I have two children. My son's name is Dragan, and my daughter's name is Sanja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask you, what is your current address?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: My current address is Kralj Aleksandra Street number 13 in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Your occupation today?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I am employed in a public state enterprise, the Serbian post office in Banja Luka -- the post office of Banja Luka, and I am working as the director of the work unit in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For a better understanding, can you tell me what is a work unit, or the work unit, how many people are working there, and what is the objective of your work?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: The public state company of the Serbian post office is organised as a centralised state company at the level of Republika Srpska. The work unit of Prijedor, where I am the director, employs about 202 workers, and it covers the region of the municipalities of Prijedor, Dubica, Nov Grad, Kostajnica, Srpski Sanski Most, and Krupa Na Uni. The main purpose or function of the company is to provide postal services in the region that I have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this detailed answer. The next question is already a kind of borderline question. May I ask, when asked in the 1991 census, what did you declare as your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: A Serb. I want to add that during that census, I worked as an instructor for the people conducting the census at the municipality level of Prijedor because I was a professional in this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: From this I understand that you were also involved in the preparation of this census. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, in the preparation and the implementation of the regulations as a technical expert associate of the committee for the census.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Tell me, you recall the ballot paper. What was it? Was there -- were there some alternatives, say, Serb, Bosniak, Croat, or also maybe related to the religion of people where they just had to crossmark one answer, or was it to the liberty to fill in whatever citizen in Prijedor Municipality wanted to fill in?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I don't remember this ballot paper very well now. But as far as I can remember, it provided a number of possibilities for the people to declare themselves as Muslims, Serbs, Croats, or Yugoslavs. And there was also the possibility in this questionnaire for people to say which faith they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Maybe we have to come back later to this census. This was only a first question on this issue. Mr. Budimir, did you hear during the last week or even the last month about the guilty plea of Ms. Plavsic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you also hear about the outcome of the case, the sentencing of Ms. Plavsic, 11 years' imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Tell me, what is your personal opinion on this outcome of the case and the mere fact that Ms. Plavsic decided to plead guilty?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: If you allow me, I graduated from the school of political sciences at the university in Zagreb. And in the times when these events took place, in view of my personal world view, I refrained from getting involved in politics, and I would now like to refrain from answering this question because it would require me to enlarge on certain issues in order to give an answer that would be satisfactory to the Trial Chamber, as an expression of my personal view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry to insist, but do you regard in principle such kind of guilty plea a way to come to reconciliation in former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: If you allow me, I will insist on refraining from answering this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Nevertheless, I want, please -- I want you to give me an answer, if it's only a yes or no. Do you believe this approach is assisting that what is our mandate, to bring and maintain peace in the area that when later on, a person arrives to that point saying "that what I did in the past was actually wrong, and I have to accept the foreseeable consequences"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Conditionally speaking, yes, but with the proviso that I mentioned before; namely, that it would require me enlarge on the events in which -- in the times concerned and provided that it applies to all the parties involved in the conflict. Then I believe it could have favourable impact in the context of the work of this Tribunal and in the context of the developments in the area in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Maybe when answering the now-following questions today, it could be helpful to bear this in mind. And no doubt, this Tribunal and this Trial Chamber doesn't see the events in 1992 and the years immediately before and afterwards in a black and white way. There is not the good and there is not the evil; we have to find out, and this is our mandate, who is individually criminally responsible for certain acts. And therefore, now, the following line of questions: For a better understanding of your personality, let's go through in a context your professional career. And by leading questions, we can go through as soon as possible this career. But before I start this line of questions, could you please tell us, have you ever been approached by one or the other party in this case? That is, on the one hand side, the Office of the Prosecutor by one or more persons, investigators, counsel, or, on the other hand, Defence counsel, Mr. Lukic, Defence counsel, Mr. Ostojic, who is absent in the moment, or one of the members of the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes. I had interviews with the team of OTP investigators. I think it was about a year ago in Banja Luka at the Intercontinental Hotel. These interviews lasted from about 8.00 a.m. to 7.00 p.m. After, that I had no more contact with the OTP, nor am I aware of the contents of that statement or the way in which it was later used by the Office of the Prosecutor. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. In addition to that, I had a brief contact with Mr. Ostojic, a short interview, on which occasion the Defence counsel asked me and my colleague, who is supposed to come in the days that follow, Mr. Travar, to testify as Defence witnesses. But we refused because we had these earlier contacts with the OTP. Further to that, I had no more contact with either party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So in conclusion, there would be one meeting is it correct, the 23rd March, 2002, from 9.00 until 5.00 in the Intercontinental Hotel in Banja Luka with the OTP. No other contact with the Prosecution. Any contact with domestic --

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No, no I didn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: -- Domestic judges?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No, I have never been in a courtroom, nor have I ever been held responsible for a misdemeanour or a crime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And to be -- are you sure that you met Mr. Ostojic and not Mr. Lukic who is present here in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I apologise if I said Mr. Ostojic. I wanted to say Mr. Lukic. I don't know Mr. Ostojic. This is the man whom I met with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you go into some details during the discussion, into details of the case with -- when speaking with the Defence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then, please, let's come to your professional career. Is it correct you completed the secondary technical school in Zagreb as well as the political sciences within the university of Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You graduated from the university of Zagreb, be it in 1984 or 1986, it doesn't matter for the purposes of this case. You did your military service in 1974 and 1975.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, also in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And then please tell us in context, what was then your professional development since 1986 until 1990?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Well, if you'll allow me to say this much, I started my career much before that, before I graduated from the university. After I completed the secondary technical school --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please understand, for the purposes of this case, we are interested only in this period of time, and especially the then-following period. So therefore, if you could concentrate first on the period between 1986-1990, and then continue telling us what you did since 1990.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: From 1986, after I graduated from the university, I found a job in the municipality of Prijedor in the municipal committee for the economy and social planning as an independent expert assistant for planning and development. Within its purview, this committee, as a municipal organ, covered the area of the economy, transport, communications and services, public services such as education, health care, information. And I was working on the development of long-term and medium-term plans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Were you subordinate to the president of the Executive Board, Mr. Vujic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No, the president of the executive council was then Mr. Vujicic, and I was subordinate to an official who was in charge of that committee, Mr. Ilija Ecim. Mr. Ilija Ecim as the public servant in charge of that commission was subordinate to Mr. Vujicic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: At the beginning of today's testimony, you mentioned that you were involved in taking the 1991 census. Could you very briefly -- we have known a lot about this, the outcome of this census.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I was not a member of the elections committee that had the task of consolidating all the data collected during the census. And as an expert, I covered only one part of the municipal territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In general terms only, the outcome was what? What was the majority in Prijedor Municipality in 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: The outcome of the census in 1992 in the Prijedor Municipality was as follows: There was an approximately equal number of Serbs and Muslims. I estimate that the Muslims were -- that the Muslims outnumbered Serbs by one or two hundred perhaps. There were much fewer Croats, and those people who declared themselves as Yugoslavs. And the number of those who declared themselves as Yugoslavs was much lower in 1991 compared to 1981.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Do you regard the outcome of this census --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. Do you regard the outcome of this census as a legal or legitimate one?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: From my point of view as an expert and from the point of view of other technical and expert assistants who were involved in the census, I believe there were many irregularities in the work and method used. Primarily because the national parties engaged people to conduct the census who did not meet the basic professional standards for this job. As a result, there were many irregularities that occurred due to lack of knowledge, lack of competence, qualification as well as conscious manipulations committed by certain members of the committee with regard to the way the census was conducted. However, since the committee was established by the municipality as a legal and legitimate one, I, as a law-abiding citizen, regarded the outcome of this census as a legitimate one despite my reservations as an expert who noticed the irregularities and deficiencies I have mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Have you ever been a member of a political party?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I was a member of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia from the time I was in high school until 1989. And after that, until 1994, I was not a member of any political party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sometimes we heard in this courtroom a witness saying he would be a passive member of a party. Would you regard yourself as a passive member of any party, or what would be your first political choice and what was your first political choice in 1991, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I was not a member of any party, and I don't think we can divide people or members into passive or active. If somebody's not involved in a political party at all, as is my case, then we cannot make these distinctions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the second part of the question, your first political choice in 1991, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: If I had a choice, I would have made it. But since I didn't, I would not like to talk about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Just try to understand your answer. Did you participate in the elections prior to April 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I did take part in the elections in 1990 as a voter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Because I don't want to go into details that's a secret vote, and therefore you have the right not to answer. Did you feel closer affiliated to one of the parties, to put it this way?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Well, if you really insist, considering the way the nominations were formed for elections at various levels, my votes depended on the ballots. And I can't say that I had strictly one political choice, that I opted clearly for one party in favour of another. It depended on the post.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Were there people in Prijedor in the beginning of 1992, or even at the end of the 1991, not accepting the outcome of the census and to a certain extent, then also not accepting the outcome of the elections in 1990?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I can't talk on behalf of other people. I accepted the legality of the elections of 1990 and the status that resulted. All of the other estimations on my part and judgements would be purely arbitrary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: To be quite concrete, did you ever know that some persons try to establish a so-called second option, or others would Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. call it "shadow government" in the beginning of 1992 because they were not satisfied with the actual political situation in Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I wasn't involved in politics in that period. And I wasn't close to the source of information that you are referring to so that I cannot clearly respond to your questions so as for my answers to really reflect the truth. But this would be more of citing information from some unreliable sources rather than providing evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to show the witness Document S394B. And always, please, put on the ELMO at the same time the English version. Have you ever seen this document before or heard about the contents of this document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then tell us, please, briefly, what was your concrete occupation in the beginning of 1992, from January to April 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: From January to April 1992, I was employed at the municipal secretariat for national defence as an expert for planning, and then later I was the assistant secretary for the civilian affairs, for civilian defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please explain, what were the functions of this secretariat for national defence or secretariat for people's defence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: The municipal secretariat for national defence based on the law of national defence forms -- is formed by the municipality so that it could carry out all the tasks relating to the administration of all issues relating to defence. It is an organ which is -- has its powers over the territory of the municipality for all issues relating to national defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Such as? Could you please give us some examples.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes. In accordance with the competencies and the powers prescribed by law, this organ carried out the following tasks: Placing military conscripts into the records so registering the military conscripts as of the age of 16 and maintaining these records of military conscripts up until the age of 60 for each individual military conscript or up to the age of 65 for the military conscripts who had the rank of officer. The organ also conducted medical examinations and the recruitment of military conscripts. Also assessed their ability to serve the regular military term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: To whom had you to report until the 1st of April 1992? What was the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: The municipal secretariat for national defence was a municipal organ for defence. And it was subordinated to the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly. But in view of the fact that this organ operated exclusively under the regulations adopted at the republican level and at the federal state level, our second-ranking organ regarding the decision-making actually was the republican secretariat for national defence. De facto, we were a municipal organ, but we operated according to regulations of the republican organ. And they were our monitoring body in terms of our implementation of those regulations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Were you a member of the Executive Board in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I was a member of the Executive Board in the period from the 30th of April until the 1st of August formally, although a change of regulations in this area, according to which we were to act, took place on the 1st of June 1992 so that formally, according to the regulations, I was a member of the Executive Board until the 1st of June, 1992. But in terms of the restructuring of this organ, from the municipal level to the republican level at the level of the defence ministry, we completed these tasks within two months, so by the 1st of August 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In this courtroom, it is an agreed fact that the 30th of April 1992 is the day of the takeover in Prijedor. You just a minute before told us that you were a member of the Executive Board as from the 30th of April 1992. Can you tell us, when did you learn for the first time that you would get this post and by whom did you learn it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I heard that two days before the Executive Board was elected. And Mr. Mico Kovacevic informed me about this during a conversation we had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When was the Executive Board elected?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I cannot remember the specific date, but I think that it was sometime in mid-April or in the first half of April, in that period sometime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was it a conversation on the four eyes you had with Mr. Kovacevic, or were others present?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Only Mr. Kovacevic was present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did he tell you when it was decided and why it was decided to elect a new Executive Board?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No. Mico Kovacevic was a simple man. And our conversation didn't last that long. He told me that there were no choices or proposals for the secretariat -- secretary of the municipal secretariat for national defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And what about the reason --

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: May I finish, please. But he asked me to accept this post in any case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Why was it necessary to have a new Executive Board as from the 30th of April?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I don't understand the formulation of the question in terms of the word "necessary."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When you obtain a new function in the Executive Board, it would be to replace another person in this position. Why was it necessary to replace another person, and whom did you replace?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: About why this was necessary, I think that the people who formed the Executive Board should give their reasons for that. As far as I'm concerned, I replaced the to then secretary of the secretariat for national defence Mr. Medunjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was Mr. Becir Medunjanin not good enough to exercise these functions, and wasn't it the result of previous elections and the decisions taken by the three main parties about the distribution of power in Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, that was the result of the division of power in the territory of Prijedor amongst the parties which won a certain amount of votes in the elections and formed the government at the municipal level. So as not to use the word "good" or "not good," in terms of carrying out the function and acting in accordance with the law, but I can responsibly state that Mr. Medunjanin never worked in the organs of the state administration before that time. He did not know what the state administration was, what laws and regulations were, and what they mean for the functioning of a state of the rule of law and equal regulations for all citizens. And he, for a year before that, since these events began to unfold in the territory of the former Yugoslavia did not implement the regulations which were in force by law which regulated the work of the municipal secretariat for national defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we shouldn't waste too much time with these kind of answers. Do you know what was the fate of Becir Medunjanin?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I think that he was a casualty of the events during the war, but I do not have specific information about what happened to him. This is all I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you read Kozarski Vjesnik?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Very little, in view of the job that I was performing, which was very dynamic with lots of duties. So that I devoted very little time to reading Kozarski Vjesnik as well as to contacts with people from the Kozarski Vjesnik, the journalists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Didn't you, in fact, read in Kozarski Vjesnik that Becir Medunjanin was arrested alive together with other members of his family?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No, I didn't read that. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Didn't you know that he had been taken to Omarska, was tortured, and then killed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No, I didn't have that information, nor did I know anything about the movements of Mr. Medunjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you hear later of the -- about the fate of Mr. Medunjanin?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I've already said that, that I found out that he was a casualty of the events during the war. But under which circumstances and when, I really have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Where did you spend the evening of the 29th of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: The evening of the 29th of April 1992, I spent in my family house in the village of Mrakovica which is about 6 kilometres away from the town of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is it your testimony here that you haven't been at Cirkin Polje on that evening, that night?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: You used the word "evening," so I responded precisely to that word "evening" which implies the time period until midnight. After midnight, around 4.00 a.m. or 4.25 a.m. that night, I was collected by a police patrol, two young men, one of whom I knew, and they told me to go with them to town. And on the way they explained to me that there was a takeover of power and that I should report to Cirkin Polje. I arrived Cirkin Polje at about 20 to 5.00 a.m., and I saw a large number of people there, most of whom I didn't know. I only knew a small number of people there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Will you please be so kind and give us the names of those persons you knew.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: The people whom I knew were the following: Mr. Srdic, Mr. Miskovic, and if I remember well, Mr. Kuruzovic, as well as this young man from the police, Mr. Jovic, the one who brought me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You are aware that there are a number of Jovics in Prijedor. Could you please give us the first name of this Mr. Jovic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Zika Jovic. He worked at the SUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you know Dr. Stakic beforehand?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No, I didn't know Dr. Stakic from before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Until the 30th of April, where did you have your office?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: My office was in a building where the municipal secretariat for national defence was, and the ministry for internal affairs. This is immediately across the street from the municipal building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Have you at least ever seen the vice-president at that time, before the 1st of May, the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor Municipality Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him. I understood the previous questions as contacts and my acquaintance with him. But I did see Mr. Stakic. Of course, I would see him on the street, over the media. I don't know. I did see him. It's not that I didn't know his face, but we didn't have any contacts before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I appreciate your precise answers. But let me come back to Cirkin Polje. Did you see Dr. Stakic as well at Cirkin Polje?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No, I didn't notice him in the crowd. I spent a very brief amount of time there. I think that I was the last person to arrive there. I was the farthest away also, so I was there for about 20 to 40 minutes. And then in the crowd created in this way, I didn't know the majority of the people. So in these milling about -- in this milling about, I didn't notice Mr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you learn later by chance and through others whether or whether not Dr. Stakic was present at Cirkin Polje that night?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear of it, nor did I discuss this topic specifically with anyone. I didn't feel that this was necessary for me for the carrying out of the duties that I was carrying out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would you tell us in some detail what happened at Cirkin Polje when people were assembled there? Did anybody take the floor, give a speech, and give an address what should happen on the next day, or actually, the same day, the 30th of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No. The previous question relating to this date and about what was going on up there, I don't have any information because I told you I arrived there the last. It was about 20 to 5.00, and already at 5.30, we set out for our jobs. And the time that I spent there, from 20 to 5.00 to 5.30, there were no talks or contacts. I believe that all the things had been clarified previously so that I did not take part in any of these conversations. There were no speeches, instructions, specific content or anything to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please explain the meaning of your sentence "I believe that all the things had been clarified previously."

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: This is what I meant, what you were talking about, whether there were any meetings, speeches, or such things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What had to be clarified previously?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't participate in the preparation or the working out, so I don't know what it was that needed to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I just had quoted your own answer. And it is not self-understanding or it's easy to get access to any kind of understanding when you immediately out of the blue tell us that you believe any of these things have been clarified previously. And then I have to insist to ask you, what were the things that had been clarified previously? To be quite concrete, the takeover?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: If you allow me, in your question, you asked me the question were there any meetings, agreements, talks about any issues. And I said I arrived at 20 to 5.00. And then after that, from the moment I arrived, there were no meetings, agreements, or conversations. And my answer wholly was directed in -- directed to replying to your question whether there were any meetings, agreements, or conversations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think the transcript speaks for itself. What happened with you, then? You told us you were there 20 to 40 minutes. Did you leave at your own or accompanied by others?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: The people who brought me, since this was in the same building, these people worked in the same building as I did, also took me back to my workplace. So I got there at about a quarter to 6.00 or 20 to 6.00, I got to the place where I was working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was it the same place as before?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I was the assistant secretary of the secretariat for national defence for civilian questions previously. And at the meeting, I was elected as secretary of the municipal secretariat for national defence. So I came to the workplace for the secretary of national defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So when arriving at about 6.00 or 20 to 6.00, you immediately took over the chair of and the office of this secretary for people's defence. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, I went to the premises of the municipal secretariat for national defence, and -- but I didn't go to that office immediately. But I went to the office where I used to be up until that time. I moved to the other office maybe two or three days later. It didn't mean anything much to me. The job could be conducted from either office, so it wasn't important to me which office I was in, and it didn't have anything to do with the actual performing of my work duties. So that time, I didn't actually go directly to that office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When taking over the work of a predecessor, one normally has a discussion, files are handed over, and there is some kind of introduction. Did you discuss these issues with Becir Medunjanin?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No, I didn't discuss those issues with Becir Medunjanin because that day, he didn't come to work. But I talked to those people who did report to the work, with the deputy, Josip Gotvald and with the other assistants for military affairs as well as other expert staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Becir Medunjanin once again? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The trial stays adjourned until 5 minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr. Budimir, to repeat: Based on your previous testimony, you are invited by the late Mico Kovacevic to take over the new position. At the same time, you mentioned later that there was a previous meeting. Was this the meeting of the Serbian Assembly of Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: My talk with Mr. Kovacevic was two days before the meeting of the Serbian Municipal Assembly of Prijedor where the Executive Board was elected in that composition headed by Mr. Kovacevic where I had the post of acting municipal secretary for national defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And you were invited by Mr. Kovacevic to attend this meeting of the Serbian Municipal Assembly of Prijedor. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kovacevic invited me to attend the session which was supposed to elect the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And where was this meeting held and who participated?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: That session was held on the premises of the public utilities institute in Prijedor, and it was attended by the deputies of the Municipal Assembly plus the nominees for the Executive Board. I attended that session together with Mr. Mico Kreco, president of the court in Prijedor, because most of the people there were unknown to me. And Mico Kreco was the only one I knew from before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You mentioned the deputies of the Municipal Assembly were there, plus other nominees. Was among these persons Dr. Milomir Stakic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: If I remember well, I think he did, but I can't say exactly. I know Mr. Kovacevic was there who told us about the nominees from the roster. I think Mr. Stakic was there, but I can't claim it with any certainty because there were many people there and they were not seated in any particular order. So I didn't really remark upon it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When you state "the deputies of the Municipal Assembly" were there in fact all the members of the Municipal Assembly, or wasn't it true that there were only the members of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I think this session was attended by all the deputies to the Municipal Assembly of Serb ethnicity, regardless of their party affiliation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Previously you mentioned that there were, in addition to these deputies being of Serb ethnicities the nominees. Nominees for what? Only nominees for posts like yours, or also nominees for other functions be it in the area of your own job or in a broader area, maybe including the Executive Board, the president of the Municipal Assembly, and so on?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Well, there were nominees who already held certain posts and who made up the Executive Board, the secretary for defence, secretary for the economy, secretary for town planning, secretary for property-related and legal affairs. Vice-president of the Executive Board, vice chairman of the assembly, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: How come that you are with a surprising precision know about these persons, but being hesitant whether one of the higher ranking persons in Prijedor, the at that time vice-president of Prijedor Municipality, attended this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Since the Executive Board was already established, I don't remember the people. I remember their posts. And I remember the holders of those posts were present. And ex officio, they were required to attend, and I wasn't. I knew only a part of those people. So I'm not speaking here about specific individualities or faces. I'm talking about the offices that had to be represented on the Executive Board and were required to attend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Since when was it planned that this Serbian Assembly should be established?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I don't know. This question does not sound very specific to me, and I can't answer it. I didn't take part in any planning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When exactly it took place?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you in the sense in which you used the term "plan." I'm talking about the day when the session was held in the first half of April. And when exactly plans were made and how, I really can't know because I have no first-hand information about it, having had nothing to do with it myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: How long were you present during this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: For the duration of the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And it took how long in hours?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I can't be very precise. I don't think, however, that it was a long one. Don't remember simply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But, sir, can't you understand that I have to ask you that it -- wouldn't it be quite natural to discuss with other persons being present there, what about this Serbian Assembly? What's the reason for creating this assembly? What is the history or the background? Because such a huge meeting can't come out of the blue.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I agree with what you say, but I have already told you that at that time, I had already made my decision to stay away from politics. I had no information about the background, and I concentrated simply on doing my job in keeping with the regulations and the law believing that adhering to the current legislation is the best I can do. As far as politics were concerned, since I had decided to keep away from them, I can't make any comments or draw conclusions. I believe the effort was focussed at the time on preserving the status quo. But I can't tell you any more than that because I was not an active participant at any level of political decision-making at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So to conclude this question, because you mentioned that the late Mico Kovacevic two days prior to the session offered you this new job, and apparently you accepted, that this meeting with the late Mr. Kovacevic would be in the beginning of April, correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes. As I have already said, it happened two days before the session. I was offered to do that part of the job, and I had very little time to decide whether to take it or not. That was difficult. I think that in the party of which Mr. Kovacevic was a member, they had no other candidate for this post. I'm talking now about the municipal secretary for national defence. Since in that period and in the period that followed, this particular office wasn't very popular. Therefore, it had to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: During this meeting, did Mr. Savanovic also participate?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: If you mean my meeting with Kovacevic, he wasn't there. But I believe he attended the session of the assembly, the session held in the public utilities institute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When and by whom did you learn that you would have to take over the new position as of 30th of April, by Mr. Kovacevic or only two days later during this meeting of the Serbian Assembly?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic told me two days in advance that I would have to take over that office, but I learned officially about it at the session of the assembly which elected me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And was already a date fixed for the new working period during this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No, there was no mention of the term of office at that meeting, and I believe the ballot papers said that people would be elected for a provisional period of six months. But there was no particular reference to it at the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For a period of six months as of?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Well, the ballot papers did not indicate the starting date. It was probably implied that time began to run as of the date of election, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. but that was an inference. There was no specific date indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But let's now go to the 29th of April. At that date, in the afternoon, say, you knew already that as from the next day, you would be in a different position?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: On that day, the 29th, I did not know that I would be taking on that job. I learned about it on the 30th at 4.30 when I arrived in town together with the police patrol that gave me a lift.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it's your testimony that you were absolutely surprised that not at midnight, but during the night police arrived at your home?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Let me tell you one thing: I had been previously elected, as we discussed just now, by the provisional composition of this assembly. But I can't say that I was absolutely surprised because due to this prior election, I wasn't completely taken aback. But the first information -- the first real information I received was when these people came to pick me up on the 30th at 4.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But then, please understand the following question: Why was it necessary to bring you first to Cirkin Polje and not immediately to your office the next day?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I don't know about that. The person who organised all that probably had their reasons. As far as I'm concerned, they could have easily taken me straight to my new office. It made no difference to me. I would have been as happy if they had driven me to my new job at 5.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Isn't it true that you received at Cirkin Polje a new ID?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I did not receive any ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We have to come back to this later. Did you receive - I know you are very precise with your answers - did you receive any other, say, permit or document allowing you to enter the premises of your office?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I don't remember clearly now if there had been any permits or, let's say per se, handed out at the moment. But in view of the situation at the time, I do not rule out the possibility. But since I already had been an employee there, I don't think I needed anything extra to go to my new job. I really can't remember precisely whether I was issued a new document. But looking back, I don't think I needed anything of the sort because as an employee, I had already been able to go in and out of the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sir, if I would ask you about what happened the 24th of April, say, 1997, I'm quite sure you couldn't answer this. So would I. But this was a very special moment. I think it didn't happen that often that you were taken during night hours by police to such an assembly and telling us now that you are not quite sure, that you don't remember precisely whether you received a new document. Can't you understand that we can't understand this?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: You know, the circumstances and the times were different. In your situation and from your position, you may well believe what you believe. But if you are wakened up at 4.30 in the morning and taken to a strange room and you know only two or three people, and you don't really understand what's going on, commotion reigns, and at a certain point they tell you go to your new jobs and start working, I don't know whether you can appreciate my answer and accept it, but I can't change anything about it. I really can't remember, and I would hate to say one way or another about something I'm not certain of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: That's just what I was trying to say. These 20 to 40 minutes were extremely special event during your life. So please, try to tell us, to the best of your recollection, first, did you receive a new document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I have to go back again to the events in my life. Since this, I had at least ten more serious events in my life than this one, more serious situations as well. But let's come back to this. I don't remember specifically whether I received any document because when I look back from today, I don't think that I was given any document, but it's possible that I was if such a document was given to others. If other people as secretaries of some other organs received such a document, then I probably received it, too. But I at the moment cannot remember whether I received any kind of document, a decision, any kind of pass or anything like that. Really, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Were there guards in front of the premises of the building where you had your office?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: In the morning when I came to the office, to my place of work, there was only one police officer at the entrance because the entrance was the same as the entrance to the Ministry of Internal Affairs. So at the entrance, there was only one police officer sitting there. From the moment that I entered the building, the police officer went back to his own place of work. There was no need for the people to be there because the situation was such that there was no need for such people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did the guard grant you immediately entrance, or did you have to present any kind of ID when entering the building?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Nothing, as far as I can remember. I didn't show anything to the guard. There was just one room where all the people of the Ministry for Internal Affairs worked. They all worked together in the same room. There was no need for me as I was coming in to show them any kind of document because those people knew me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. A more general question: This 30th of April 1992, who else was replaced in the Municipality of Prijedor by whom? Let us start with your own office, and then go to other areas.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: In the organ that I worked in, only Mr. Medunjanin was replaced. And I came to the post of the municipal -- to the post of secretary of the municipal secretariat for national defence. In the rest of the hierarchy, nobody else was replaced from the post that they were performing. If we're thinking about the municipal secretariat for national defence, which is where I worked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What about the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: As far as the Municipal Assembly is concerned, I think all of the officials of Muslim or Croat ethnicity were replaced. I'm not quite sure. I'm only talking about the officials now. But the deputies of those officials, I think, were not all replaced. I don't have the specific information, but I don't believe that all of the deputies were replaced at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What about the presidency of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: There was no presidency of the Municipal Assembly. There was just the president and the vice-president. I think the vice-president took over the functions of the president.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And why this? Why was this necessary?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I don't know why. I don't know why this was necessary. Probably those people who organised that should be asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you know Professor Cehajic as a resident in that area?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him. I knew Professor Cehajic as a professor from the high school, even though I didn't go to that high school. I knew him; I knew his face; I knew what he looked like. But nothing more than that. I didn't have any other contacts with Mr. Cehajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sir, do you want to tell us as you sit here today that you didn't know at that day Professor Cehajic was replaced by Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I didn't say that. Perhaps the translation was wrong. I said that the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly took over the post of president.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you ever see Professor Cehajic after the 30th of April again?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you hear about his fate?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I heard that he came to a tragic end in those events, but I don't Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. have information as to the circumstances, when and where and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Just a moment ago, you emphasised that you discussed the replacement of officials in the Municipal Assembly only. What about officials in other areas in the Municipality of Prijedor? What about replacement in these other areas?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I didn't say that I talked about the replacement, but I just noted which replacements had been made. I didn't have any discussions or conversations about that. I don't know which other replacements do you mean? Could you please be more specific. And if I have any knowledge about that, if I know anything about that, then I can answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it's the best way to put to you your own answer, you said: "But I just noted which replacements had been made." So please, tell us which replacements had been made? What did you note?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I noted that all officials from the municipality, at the municipality level, had been conducted, and I said that I was not sure whether any of the deputies of those officials at that point were replaced or all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Once again, what was the reason that these replacements happened, based apparently on a night meeting immediately after that the next morning and prepared on the meeting you participated of the so-called Serbian Assembly of Prijedor Municipality? Why was this necessary?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: In that context, I can answer with some general and generally accepted reasons. But I would like to refrain as far as any of my own personal qualifications and political assessments are concerned. As far as the general matters are concerned, probably the Serbs wanted to maintain the status quo of the existing situation. They believed it was legal and legitimate for them to apply the existing legal regulations. And in that context, they held the referendum about remaining in the existing state, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. While on the other hand, members of the other two ethnic groups held a referendum on the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and later in that context, the Lisbon talks were held where the generally accepted position was about some type of cantonisation of Bosnia and Herzegovina which would imply the satisfaction of the interests of all of the three peoples. This agreement was signed by all the participants. And then later, the representatives of the Muslim people withdrew their signature which in a way, in the light of all the previous events from 1991, was an introduction into the way things would go in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And in that context, also the events that were talked about. But once again, let me say I am a politologist by profession, but at that time I did not wish to be active in politics and I would kindly request this Chamber not to -- to allow me to abstain from answering questions or providing answers on political matters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You're here not as an political expert; you're here as a witness on concrete facts. To come to other concrete questions, what was the function of the Council for National Defence and who were the members?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: In accordance with the law on general people's defence, which was adopted in 1983, the Council for National Defence is an advisory body of the Municipal Assembly. And therefore, in accordance with the law, it deals with the relevant questions pertaining to national defence. And in that sense, provides its positions and its recommendations to the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Who were the members?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Members, in accordance with the regulations of the law, members of the executive council were the president of the Executive Board; and in accordance with that law, because there were no amendments which regulated the body of -- the work of this body, the members were the members of the municipal council of the League of Communists, the president of the socialist council -- alliance, also the president of the veterans' association, the president of the youth association, the commander of the Territorial Defence, and other members appointed by the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Were you --

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: The secretary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: -- A member?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: The secretary of the municipal secretariat by his function is the secretary of that body in accordance with this law that I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you participate in a meeting of the Council for National Defence, any of them or several of them?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I did participate in the body -- in the work of this body. I think I participated in the work -- several meetings. I cannot specify how many, but in some way by my function I was a member of that body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May the witness please be shown Exhibit S60, 6-0. Can we please see this document in a way that we can start from the top of the entire document. Could you please comment on this document. Is it correct that there was the 4th meeting of the Council for National Defence of the Prijedor Municipal Assembly held on 15 may 1992 starting at 1000 hours? Do you recall this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I think that this is a meeting of the 15th of May, according to the minutes that I have in front of me. Whether this was the fourth meeting or not, I don't know. I don't know when you would count this body as starting its operation, but the minutes do state that it is the fourth meeting of the Council for National Defence of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... my question. Because this is our minutes of the fourth meeting. When was the first meeting of this Council for National Defence, to the best of your recollection only, of course?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: This question requires a slightly longer answer. When I told you something about the constituting of this body and what it states in the law about this body, I cannot specifically tell you when the first meeting was held of the Council for National Defence because this body, I don't remember this body being formed at a meeting of the municipal council after the multiparty elections. I even think that it was not formed at that point, but by analogy and the order of events, it was multiparty Municipal Assembly and the previous president, Mr. Cehajic, held some meetings of the council which I did not attend at the time because I was not a member of that body then. So that I cannot specifically tell you when which meeting was held. And I cannot talk about the chronology of the events, whether it was the fourth meeting, when the previous meetings were held, and what exactly was discussed at those meetings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And please, in the next line, you can read: "Dr. Milomir Stakic, president of the council, chaired the meeting." Why was it that Dr. Milomir Stakic was the president of this Council for National Defence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: In view of the law that I have referred to and which was not changed in the meantime, the president of the Council for National Defence, by his position, was the president of the assembly. So probably that is why he chaired the meetings of the Council for National Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So let's go through the persons who attended this meeting. Dr. Milomir Stakic, Dr. Milan Kovacevic. What was his position?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: President of the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Simo Miskovic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please always help us with the function of these persons. Simo Miskovic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Simo Miskovic was the president of the executive council of the Prijedor SDS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Vladimir Arsic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: He was the commander of the 43rd Motorised Brigade which had its headquarters at the Prijedor garrison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Pero Colic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Colic was the commander of the 5th Brigade which was also based in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Slobodan Kuruzovic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I think that at the time, Mr. Kuruzovic was the commander of the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Radmilo Zeljaja.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Radmilo Zeljaja I think had the rank of captain at that point, but I don't know whether -- what function he was performing at the 43rd Motorised Brigade in the Prijedor garrison. He was an assistant of Arsic, so I'm not sure what function he was performing at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Rade Javoric.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Rade Javoric was also the commander of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then your name follows. After this, Simo Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: He was the chief of the public security station in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Cedo Sipovac.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: He was the chief of the military territorial organ for mobilisation at the Prijedor garrison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Vojo Pavicic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: He was the secretary of the municipal secretariat for housing and urban affairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Bosko Mandic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Bosko Mandic was the vice-president of the Executive Board and commander of the municipal staff of the TO, as a member of the staff. He was the commander of the municipal staff for civilian defence. Mr. Bosko Mandic was the commander of the municipal staff for civilian defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Ranko Travar.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: He was the secretary of the secretariat for economy and social affairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Milenko Rajlic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: He was the secretary for information in the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Dragan Savanovic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: He was the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Spiro Marmat.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: He was an expert in the secretariat for national defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you meet one of these persons we can see starting with Dr. Stakic, concluding with the name of Spiro Marmat, during the last four weeks, see or meet, that there's no misunderstanding?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Over the past four weeks, I met Mr. Ranko Travar, Bosko Mandic, and Dragan Savanovic. And allow me once again just to check. I see Mr. Pavicic, but I'm not sure whether in the time period that you are talking about that I had been with him. But I do have contacts with him, and over the past month or two, I did meet him. But in the relevant period, I don't remember that I had any business or any other contacts with him. As far as the other people are concerned, I did meet them frequently. Mr. Savanovic and Mr. Travar, I do have contacts with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you discuss with them your testimony here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No, except with Mr. Travar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you prepare your testimony together with Mr. Travar?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No, we did not particularly prepare for testifying. But we did exchange information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What kind of information, please?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Well, we contacted each other when we received this paper. We received it together. We went together to the police station. We prepared the records together with the girl who was the interpreter. We filled in the questionnaires together. And the text is identical, both -- almost identical for both of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On page 42, line 8, you mentioned that Mr. Spiro Marmat was an expert in the secretariat for national defence. He participated in this meeting in this capacity?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And at the same time, he kept the minutes. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I believe so, because that's what it says in the -- on the paper. I don't see why it would be written there otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When did you see or meet Mr. Spiro Marmat the last time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Well, in the last three or four or even five months, I didn't see him. He worked until recently in the ministry in Prijedor. He's now retired, and his family lives in Belgrade. So he commutes between Prijedor and Belgrade. In the past six months, I had no contact with him in particular, apart from perhaps seeing him in passing in the street. We had no contact in the period in question. While we worked together, of course, we saw each other every day. I stopped working in 1997, 1998. Since then, we haven't seen much of each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We have to come back to this later. May I ask the usher, please, to forward the document a little bit that we can read the lower part. You can see the agenda, that due to this paper, was confirmed. First, decision on the organisation and functioning of the Crisis Staff. Could you please explain what was the reason to organise and function the Crisis Staff. Apparently, it was Dr. Milomir Stakic and you yourself participating in the debate as the only interventors.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I think this is about a draft decision which came from upstairs, probably from the level of the president or the presidency to form Crisis Staffs on the municipal level. This decision said what exactly a Crisis Staff is supposed to do and indicated recommended members. I think it was a document which came down from higher up. I had nothing to do with it, and I, as a secretary, had to accept this and forward this decision in that form to the assembly without giving my own opinion on it. The assembly was supposed to consider and deliberate on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So you received this order to establish a Crisis Staff and forwarded it to this group meeting there, the 15th of May. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No, I did not receive the decision on the organisation and functioning of the Crisis Staff. It's the president who receives such decisions from higher organs. I mean, the president of the Municipal Assembly. We were only supposed to forward it to the assembly for review and adoption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it would be Dr. Stakic receiving this order, and it would then for you and the other participants to forward this order. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic received instructions in the form of that decision. The board reviewed the decision and decided that there was nothing to change in it, but rather that it should be forwarded to the assembly for adoption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You vaguely mentioned that apparently this came from persons in higher places. Wasn't it the president of the state who gave this order?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I already said it was the head of the state or president of the presidency. I can't say exactly, but it is my estimate that it must have come from that level because as far as I know, there was the president of the state and a presidency consisting of three members. Who the head of the presidency was at that time, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
