utterances.text: When you were asked by the Prosecution during the interview the 23rd of March 2002, on page 11, you stated, line 15: "After the Executive Board was disbanded, the Crisis Staff of the Municipal Assembly was formed by the decision of the president of the state, and I was a member due by virtue of my position of secretary of the secretariat." At that point in time, you spontaneously answered that "It was the decision of the president of the state." Does this refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Well, I have to tell you that even if I said so at the time, I'm still not sure whether it was the head of state or the presidency. I cannot recollect that with any certainty, but I don't see what it changes anyway, whether it was the president or the presidency. I only meant that it came from the highest -- from the supreme body and that we, as lower organs, had to abide by it and put it into practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you yourself see this order establishing the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I believe the president of the municipality held it in his hands and read it out to us. I never held the paper myself. I can't remember now exactly who was it who read the decision and signed it. I believe the president read it out to us. There were no comments, and there were no proposed amendments before adoption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And then how did you achieve the goal to forward this order to other persons, as you mentioned just beforehand? Wasn't this document copied, and isn't it true that this document was signed by Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I don't rule out the possibility that Dr. Karadzic signed it. I said it was either Dr. Karadzic or the presidency, but even if it came from the presidency, it had to be signed by Dr. Karadzic, either in his capacity as head of state or in his capacity of president of the presidency. It was forwarded, in any case, to the municipal level, to the president of the Municipal Assembly and the secretary, and the technical bodies involved because it was their job to review it and forward it for adoption. I did not have anything with the review of this decision because that was in the competence of the appropriate bodies of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On the document, it reads, after the name participating in the discussion, Dr. Stakic and you, Mr. Budimir, "The following conclusion was adopted: First, the draft on the organisation and functioning of the Crisis Staff is approved under the proviso that a representative of the garrison in Prijedor be added to the proposed lists of members of the Crisis Staff." Why this? Why was it necessary to go even beyond this order and to add a representative of the garrison in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I don't know. It was probably not my proposal as an expert. It was probably the proposal of an official who thought that it was important to do so. But in view of the instructions that came from upstairs, this proposal was not accepted, and these people were not appointed to the Crisis Staff. I don't know for what reasons, and I don't know whether there had been any additional consultations. This proposal may have been made, but the Executive Board was not allowed -- was not authorised to change the composition of the Crisis Staff as proposed by the presidency or the president.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be logic -- then when you state that it was not your proposal and only two persons participated in the discussion, that this proposal was one of Dr. Milomir Stakic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Well, it turns out to be logical, but I can't claim that with any certainty. I don't know with what accuracy the records were made. I'm not sure that only two persons participated in this discussion. There may have been more. And only on the basis of the record, I can't draw the conclusion that it was Mr. Stakic's proposal if it wasn't mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you ever have reasons to believe that Mr. Spiro Marmat kept the minutes not in the most appropriate and conscientious way?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: That's not what I meant. But I believe that every person who is making notes or taking a record of a meeting is writing down only the most important things and not covering absolutely all the details of a discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then let's go to the second point of the agenda, please. "Mobilisation in the municipality." You can see from this document that apparently you participated, and you were the first one taking the floor during the meeting. And then we see the conclusions noting that also Dr. Milomir Stakic participated in the discussion. So here, it reads: "No Crisis Staff can be formed in companies or other legal entities." Was this decision enforced?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: To be quite honest, many decisions of the Crisis Staff were never enforced. The Crisis Staff made its decisions in the form of conclusions and recommendations and all the other forms taken over from the Municipal Assembly. But it had no instruments to ensure the implementation of its decision, even as regards companies. I certainly took part in these discussions because that was part of my job, and it falls within the competencies of the secretariat for national defence. But all issues that had to do with mobilisation are very specific to that time when the mobilisation took place. Mobilisation was carried out within the JNA much earlier, in 1991, in September. The way they were mobilised, through callups, through military territorial bodies, and sent to Slavonia where they spent from September 1991 to March or April 1992. Also there was mobilisation of the Territorial Defence that was carried out from September 1991 to April 1992, plus the mobilisation of the reserve force of the police. So practically mobilisation covered all the structures and included all the people employed in companies who had wartime assignments. So mobilisation was completed within that period. And at this point we are talking about, it was only a matter of reviewing the strength of units that came back from Slavonia, the 3rd, 4th, and 5th unit, and units were not complete for the reasons you are already aware of, because Muslims and members of other ethnic communities did not respond to mobilisation callups. And also because these units had suffered losses. So the actual strength was only 50 per cent of what it should have been, according to establishment. And these units had to be reinforced and supplied with military conscripts and materiel and equipment. That's what we were talking about at this session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would Muslims and members of other ethnic communities be welcomed in JNA or TO in 1992? We are speaking now about the 15th of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Well, as for being welcome or not, I worked in a body that worked strictly in keeping with the law. The law said that all the people in the territory covered by that organ were required to respond to the callup, and that applied in 1991 during the first mobilisation and during the entire period when conscripts were mobilised. Upon the return of these units from Slavonia, the units still included members of other ethnic communities, Muslims and Croats, although in smaller numbers. As far as the Territorial Defence and the police are concerned, we did not resolve the matters completely at all because until the outbreak of the conflict, these units included a half of Muslims and the rest were Serbs and Croats. At the moment when the conflict broke out, the composition of the units changed. These units were in charge of taking control of the territory and were maintained in the new percentage. But there were, again, rifts along ethnic lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Tell me, coming to point 3 of the agenda, what was the reason to start the transformation of both TO staffs and form a unified command for control and command of all the units formed in the territory of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Well, to explain the reason in detail would take time. It is my opinion that sometime around that time, the system of the Territorial Defence in Bosnia and Herzegovina broke up. According to the law, these units were formed on the level of Bosnia and Herzegovina and were commanded by the commander of TO along the principles of single command and absolute obedience from lower levels. However, when this general rift occurred in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, it was reflected also on command and control. And the units of the Territorial Defence which remained in the territory held by Muslims were used to form the BH army, and the TO units remaining in Serb territory were resubordinated to the JNA, later the VRS. And that is the subject of that discussion at the session of the assembly which discussed the need to resubordinate these units because it is a well-known fact that you cannot have two or more armies operating in the same area. That is one of the basic principles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So in conclusion, you regard it as the responsibility to decide on this issue on the level of the municipality of Prijedor. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No, that is not what I thought, nor is it true. For this level of command and control, it was within the purview of the higher organs such the assembly. The assembly through the competent body, the national defence secretariat, dealt with it, and conducted reorganisation, transformation, and resubordination of these units, whereas the municipal level had nothing to do with it. It was too low for this sort of decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: How was it, then, possible that you during this discussion on Prijedor level took the conclusion to start the unification of both TO staffs?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Well, we were just reviewing events in our area. And in view of the decisions from higher organs, we issued decisions to implement instructions from higher bodies. We could not be separate from the overall system of organisation and we couldn't review in Prijedor and Banja Luka and other municipalities different issues. We all reviewed mainly one and the same thing. We are the body who -- we were the body who had the right to make proposals to the assembly and come up with initiatives about the implementation of conclusions and decisions from above in the most efficient manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's please turn to the next issues on the agenda, briefly. May I ask the usher to change the document. You can see on agenda point 4, it is disarmament of paramilitary formations. These were paramilitary formations of all ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: As regards the disarmament of all paramilitary formations, this is what I can tell you: With the return of units from Slavonia, namely, the 43rd and the 5th Brigade, there appeared a large concentration of armed men of all ethnicities in our area. There were about 1.950 people, according to establishment, half Muslims, half Serbs approximately. And if you add to that the police which had a force of about 1400 people, again, according to establishment, it was considered that we had a large number of armed men in our territory counting only those who were legally mobilised. And our desire was that these people, who were mobilised as the reserve force, should be downsized. In addition to that, again, there were uncontrolled groups that could not be controlled by either the army or the police. And our wish was to disarm these people and to have only the army in the barracks with a strength envisaged by the establishment, the regular members of the Territorial Defence staff, and reserve policemen as envisaged by the establishment which was significantly increased from 1991 to 1992, from 700 to 800 hundred to 1500, and we also wanted to downsize the number of the reserve policemen because we thought it was enough for law enforcement in the municipality. And we thought the large number of armed men could cause problems and was an accident waiting to happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's finally turn to the last point of the agenda. "Taking over the duties of the military department. Slavko Budimir and Dr. Milomir Stakic participated in the discussion. After the discussion, the following conclusion was adopted: The municipal secretariat for national defence is requested to prepare for the Municipal Assembly executive committee a draft staffing table for the secretariat which shall include the tasks taken over from the military department." And then signed by the president of the National Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Regarding the terminology here, the military department is actually a military territorial organ formed by the former JNA sometime in 1991 while the mobilisation was being carried out, when members of other ethnic groups did not respond to the callup and when the authorised body of the municipal secretariat headed by Mr. Medunjanin at that time did not act in accordance with the regulations which were then in force. So they did not carry out the mobilisation, even though they were supposed to do that under the law. And they didn't do it for reasons known only to them. So in order to staff the units, the army formed military territorial organs whose tasks were the same as those of the municipal secretariat for national defence. Actually, they took over those duties and conducted the callup independently with the documents that they had at their disposal, with the appeals of the Crisis Staff and the Municipal Assemblies, appealing to the conscripts to report to their places of assembly. Since this was not enough, the secretariats also conducted the tasks of mobilisation and resupply. Since the municipal secretariat for national defence continued to act in accordance with the existing laws in that territory because the other organs were not acting in accordance with the regulations, there was no need for two bodies to be carrying out the same work. So the documents and -- which were at the military body were transferred to the secretariat which continued to carry out all the mobilisation duties until the systematisation draft proposal was made which would then be submitted to the Municipal Assembly for adoption to the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Finally, nobody objected to this part of the agenda and the conclusions adopted. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Are you thinking about this last topic that I talked about? No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then it is necessary to take a short break now. The trial stays adjourned until 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. We're still with the same document where the agenda, point 1, decision on the organisation and functioning of the Crisis Staff. Could you please tell us, was this the first point in time when it was discussed to establish a Crisis Staff in Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I think that they are. I don't have any other information. It's true I don't remember, but I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you at this meeting already take conclusions about the final composition of this Crisis Staff, not only in terms of functions but also with concrete names?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I don't remember whether at that point, along with the decision, there was also the list of the functions comprising the Crisis Staff. But I know that one of the documents, whether in the follow-up regulations or -- I don't know if that came together with the decision. But there was a document there which specified the posts comprising the Crisis Staff. And of course, the people who carry out those functions by the very nature of that are part of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May the witness then be shown, please, Document S180B. A to be put on the ELMO. And may I at the same time ask the audio-video unit, is the video to be played - this would be Exhibit S7 - prepared? Please start the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Stop. Could you please try to fix the video a little bit that we can identify -- yes. Who is sitting around this table, please? Starting from the right-hand side, the person wearing glasses. We are now at 11:36:30:23.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I cannot identify the first person or the second. The third person I think is Mr. Macura. Next to Mr. Macura, I think, is the vice-president of the assembly, Mr. Savanovic. Next to him, I am sitting. And then next to me is Mr. Stakic. On the left side, it's unclear, so I'm unable to identify the persons. The first person on the right side, it looks like Mr. Pavic, the chief of the civilian defence, but I'm not sure. He's my colleague, and he's like me, and he wears glasses. But I cannot say with certainty whether that is him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could the video please be winded forward a little bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Stop. It's now easier to identify the three persons to the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Mr. Bosko Mandic, vice-president of the Executive Board. The first person next to me is Mr. Zeljaja. Behind him, I think, leaning on his hand is journalist Mutic. The person with the glasses is a person who was up at the command of the brigade, and he came together with Mr. Zeljaja. And to tell you the truth, I cannot remember the last name of that man. I think he was a lieutenant-colonel or a colonel. I know him, but I cannot remember his surname.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please wind forward, the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Stop. And we are now with 11:36:38:03. You can identify the three persons to the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Miskovic, Mr. Kuruzovic, and I think that the last person is Mr. Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Please wind forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Stop. These two persons would be? 11:36:48:04.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: From left to right, Mr. Kovacevic, Mr. Pavicic, and Mr. Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Stop. And now, we can see the other end of the same table. From left to right, you mentioned already that you don't recall the name of the person wearing uniform and glasses at the same time. The next person from the left-hand side? At 11:36:56:22. Who would be this person also wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Zeljaja. Next to him is Mr. Travar. And next to Mr. Travar is Mr. Marmat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would the assumption be correct that this is a meeting of the Crisis Staff of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I cannot draw such a conclusion about what meeting this is. But I think that it is not a meeting of the Crisis Staff in view of the presence of Mr. Miskovic. And the military member, I think that they did not attend so frequently. Mr. Zeljaja or Mr. Arsic were there more often. I don't remember this other man being there a lot. And I think that I could not really say. I think that this is probably more the council, all the more so because the minutes are done by Mr. Marmat while the meetings of the Crisis Staff were taken down by Mr. Baltic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Please forward the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Stop. Thank you. This concludes this video. You still have before you the document S180. If you could please be so kind and open page number 36, item number 19. That's the decision on appointments to Prijedor municipal Crisis Staff at its meeting 22nd May 1992 by the Prijedor Municipal Assembly. Does this document, after your perusal, correctly reflect the composition of Prijedor Municipal Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, except under number 10, Zeljko Macura. I don't know who compiled the decision later and to what extent this was, but I feel that this man was not in the document setting out the members of the Crisis Staff, nor was he so by his function. He was a doctor in the 43rd Prijedor Motorised Brigade. So I don't know how he ended up here. I believe that he was not a member of the staff, unless this was something along the lines of Dr. Kovacevic or Dr. Stakic with Dr. Macura. I don't know how he ended up on this list, in what capacity. These other names above correspond to the posts and the people appointed as members of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And these documents would be to sign -- to be signed by the president of the Municipal Assembly. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Probably, if that's what's indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just note that on the document, the decision number 19 Your Honour has read, I believe we brought this to your attention before, but the translation is clearly wrong as to the date. The B/C/S has the date May 20th, for some reason the translation says May 22nd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I'm aware of this problem. I just wanted to come back to this with the follow-up question: When, in fact, was the first meeting of the Crisis Staff in Prijedor Municipality? When you have a glance, please, on the cover page of this Official Gazette of 25 June 1992, issue number 18, there it reads that "At the session of 20 May, 1992, the decision was adopted on the organisation and work of Prijedor Municipal Crisis Staff," which would be the implementation of the previous decision of 15th of May. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: This is a decision about the organisation and the work of the Crisis Staff adopted by the Municipal Assembly whereby the Crisis Staff is appointed of the 20th. The previous issue that we talked about was the draft proposal from the council of national defence of the 15th of May. And then this proposal was passed on to the assembly for adoption. I don't know whether the Crisis Staff meeting was held on the same day that it was formed or whether it was held on the next day or so. It's something that I really cannot tell you specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It was very close to this decision of 20 May 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I believe that the staff meeting was after this decision because the meeting could not have been held until it was appointed by the Municipal Assembly. So whether the meeting was on the first, second, or third day after the adoption is something I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: How often did the Crisis Staff meet?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: It's difficult to be specific about that, especially if we're talking about the term "frequently." The staff met as necessary, simply in the -- according to the decision of the person who headed the staff. If he felt that such a meeting was necessary, he would consult with the other people, and then a staff meeting would be scheduled. I don't know whether this was every seven or ten or fifteen days, but generally that was the time period that they were held.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So the president would be responsible for conferring the Crisis Staff and the agenda of the Crisis Staff. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: The president of the municipality convened the Crisis Staff meetings according to his assessment and after consulting with the other members, particularly members of the Executive Board and members of the secretariat. And that is also how the agenda was prepared, with consultations with those other people, depending on the problems or issues that those people felt should be reviewed by the staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Budimir, on the top page of this Official Gazette, it reads, "Year I" even though we have seen Official Gazettes of Prijedor Municipality in the previous years. Why was this, that in 1992 started with "Year I"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I don't explain it at all. In view of the competencies and duties of the organ that I was, we didn't have any Official Gazettes, so I didn't have any insight into what certain markings meant nor how these were given to the Gazette. I can talk specifically about what was in the jurisdiction of the -- of my organ. But this is really outside of that area, so I cannot really tell you anything specific about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Where did you meet?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Are you thinking of the Crisis Staff or...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right, Crisis Staff meeting.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: The staff usually met on the premises -- it met in the small conference hall next to the hall and the office where the president of the assembly was carrying out his functions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Where else did the Crisis Staff meet, please?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff mostly met in that room. And if you permit me, I would just like to say, besides the fact that the Crisis Staff met and worked in meetings, the Crisis Staff had 24-hour duty call. So there was a reporting centre that was formed in the basement of the Municipal Assembly building where this centre for alerting was situated before. And this centre operated under my jurisdiction. It was part of my job. Information was received there from the civilian aspects of life in the municipality, and those pieces of information that were relevant for the work of the Crisis Staff were passed on to the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So would it be correct that there was a night shift and a day shift?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Duty service in the municipal centre for alerting was permanent, 24 hours a day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And who met there? Only members of the Crisis Staff as such, as we see it from the document, from the Official Gazette, or also other individuals?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No. They -- the members of the Crisis Staff did not attend in this form, as it is indicated there. The centre for alerting was manned by technical and expert people, employees of the secretariat for national defence, and they did their duties, taking shifts 24 hours a day. I spent the most time there of all the members of the Crisis Staff because it was in the jurisdiction of the municipal secretariat for national defence, and Mr. Ranko Travar was often there. Considering the fact that the information gathered there fell mostly within the province of the organ headed by Mr. Travar, namely, the economy and social services. Information about these aspects of life flowed into this centre, and we together sorted out and selected information trying to remove and redress the problems that we could as soon as possible, whereas other information was processed and forwarded to the Crisis Staff for further action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did the Crisis Staff have other special buildings in Prijedor dedicated to the execution of the necessary work of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff worked in meetings. It had no special premises of its own, apart from this room where they met. All other municipal organs and agencies served the Crisis Staff doing the job that was legally prescribed to them, and everyone had their offices in the municipal building where they carried out their jobs as prescribed by the regulations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What about the building in Cirkin Polje?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I don't know. After I left my office in that building, I never again visited Cirkin Polje, and not a single session that I attended was held in that building. What happened to that building, who received it for use later, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do you know about the issuing of certificates or vouchers for fuel?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: You have to know the volume of the work I handled, which was very complex and difficult, and I can easily say, very unpopular, so I had lots of trouble doing my job, having a lot of contacts with war profiteers and other abusers. So all these other things such as abuses of vouchers of fuel were not handled by me. It was in the competence of the secretary for the economy and other people. So I don't have enough information to tell you how it was done upstairs and how it was handled. I did not actively take part in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In Article 2 on the decision of the organisation and work of the Prijedor municipal Crisis Staff, it reads: "Prijedor municipal Crisis Staff has been established to coordinate the functions of the authorities, the defence of the municipal territory, the protection of safety of people and property, the establishment of government, and the organisation of all other fields of life and work." What about the influence of the Crisis Staff on the military forces?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff was set up to coordinate all the functions of the government and defence of the territory, as it says here. From the viewpoint of organisation, we all know exactly what government means and which organs are involved. This organ performed the combined functions of the government, and there were laws and bylaws regulating other aspects of life which remained in force. That means that this staff had no competencies over the army, the police, or other defence structures because they acted in keeping with other laws that continued to be in force and to govern their functioning, that is, the law on national defence and the law on internal affairs. They were required to implement these laws. This decision does not render these laws null and void. Therefore, the Crisis Staff had no opportunity to rule these structures. It could only exchange information with the army, not influence it. The same goes for the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the usher, please, on the same document, S180, to open page 51, issue 48. How can you bring in conformity your previous answer with this order of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't have the order in front of me. The monitor is showing the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The B/C/S should be the same pagination.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Can I start answering now, or do you have any more questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I still stand by my view that the Crisis Staff had no authority to take decisions, issue orders, or resolve any matters regarding the army or the police because these structures were governed very precisely by other laws.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I interrupt you. The question is -- may I interrupt you. The question is not what under the law is possible, but what actually happened. And you recall this order of the 17th of June 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I remember it. It was one of the rare occasions of the sort, and I remember the deliberations on this issue. But I don't remember this order, and I'm seeing it for the first time in this form. That's what I wanted to comment upon. From the formal and legal point of view, I explained what was possible and what was not. As for this issue and this issue order, the Crisis Staff, in view of the situation and the problems encountered, and this was one of the rare occasions where we discussed these matters, simply because the problems in town were so bad that this situation could not be tolerated any longer. And we asked from -- people from the army and the police to re-establish law and order and to prevent the looting, the robberies, the disorder, and unrest that was going on in town. Normally, the army and the police should have done so of their own accord. But the practice was different. So we asked the representatives of the army and the police to form teams made up of the existing members, the existing force, who were supposed to enforce law anyway but were not doing it. And we simply urged them to put a stop to it. I don't know why somebody formulated this request in the form of an order. As far as I know, there was no discussion to that effect and nobody had instructions to write such an order, and I don't see how anybody could have taken it upon themselves to do something that they were not required to do by law. We were simply making a request of the army and the police. I don't know why this was written in the form of an order. This question should better be put to the secretary of the municipality whose job it was to take care of the legality of municipal orders -- municipal organs and their work and follow the decisions of the Municipal Assembly in keeping with the law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When I ask you now the same question related to other documents - may I ask the usher to turn to page 69, issue number 97 - would you please be so kind and with a view to the remaining time, please, a brief answer only. How is it possible that by a decision taken in Prijedor, the Serbian TO shall be incorporated into the structure of the region and placed under its command?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: That is not possible either. According to the law and in view of the discussion about this, such a conclusion was not formulated because it was impossible to formulate it in such language. It could only have been done according to a decision of the assembly on the reorganisation of staffs of Territorial Defence. By decision of higher organs to issue a recommendation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, but once again, I don't want to hear what is possible under the law that we can find out ourselves. The problem is do you recall this -- the discussion on this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: There was discussion on the resubordination of TO units to army units, but there was no order or conclusion adopted by us. But we could only make a recommendation to the assembly for this to be put into practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You're aware that we are reading from the Official Gazette. May we turn now to page number 54, issue 55, please. Please, also brief comments on this.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I don't remember whether this happened at a session of the Crisis Staff, but from what the law said about that previously, I really can't answer this briefly. I would have to elaborate my explanation which the time does not allow. But if you want a brief answer, I don't remember that this was said at the session of the Crisis Staff, and I don't remember that such a decision was made. But the whole system worked in such a way that approval had to be obtained from upstairs, including approval of the republican Territorial Defence staff. So it couldn't be forwarded to the assembly without the approval of the competent commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So who would be in charge of getting this approval?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: That would be the commander of the republican Territorial Defence, but in this particular case, there was no republican TO commander on the BH level. So the person in question was the Territorial Defence commander in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't need S180 any longer. May we please have S173. Please in B/C/S, always the best possible copy, that is, a colour copy. May it please be moved a little bit upwards. You see two signatures on this document.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You are acquainted with the signature of Dr. Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I can't say. I have seen his signature before, but I can't identify it here. I believe Mr. Kovacevic's signature was a bit longer on certain documents I've seen. So I'm not quite certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What about the signature of Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't identify Dr. Stakic's signature here. There is a variety of signatures by Dr. Stakic that I've seen. This doesn't look to me like his signature. I can't identify it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Who would be the one who would have to sign a document in the absence of Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Ex officio, it would be vice-president of the municipality, Mr. Savanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May the witness please be shown the other document, please, remaining there, S267. Do you recognise this signature "za"? Then followed by a very special signature.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This would be the signature of whom?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I think, because it is rather idiosyncratic with this half circle, it is Dragan Savanovic's signature. Anyway, I had more to do with documents signed by Savanovic than by Dr. Stakic. And judging by this little circle, I think it is his signature. I think he still signs himself this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May the witness then be shown, and the others be left there, S70, 7-0. For Madam Registrar, the next one would be S174-1B. Can you please explain the signature and stamp you can see there.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: The stamp is that of the Municipal Assembly, but I cannot identify the signature or explain to whom it could belong. This is, I believe, the old stamp of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor before all these events. But when I compare these two signatures, I am not sure of anything any more. I don't know who -- which one belongs to whom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do you recall the conclusion measures to blockade the town shall continue to be in force? Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: To be quite frank, I really don't know. In what sense do you mean, the blockade?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I don't remember it. Blockade is a very broad sense. That would mean closing off the entire territory. The way it is formulated here it would have to be more specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... my question was did you participate in the meeting when it was discussed that the blockade of the town should continue to be in force? Do you recall this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I don't remember this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did at any point in time Dr. Stakic not participate in a meeting of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I can't say that with any accuracy. Maybe he failed to attend a session or two, but if he wasn't there, then Mr. Savanovic took over as vice-president of the assembly and deputy chairman of the Crisis Staff. It may have happened, since it was also regulated by a decision who was his stand-in, and that was Mr. Savanovic as vice-president.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I asked you a concrete question, how often it was that Dr. Stakic did not preside over the Crisis Staff when there was a meeting of the Crisis Staff? Please don't try to circumvent the answers.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Well, I really can't tell you precisely whether it happened two, three, or five times, if he was away on a business trip or something, he could have missed a session of the Crisis Staff. But how often it happened, two, three, or five times, I don't know, because I didn't keep records about that. It was not my job to keep records of who attended the sessions, who didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The other way around: Dr. Stakic in principle, save the exceptions you just mentioned, presided over the Crisis Staff and was present during the meeting of Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was there any separate group within the Crisis Staff holding separate meetings, maybe as it often happens in political circles, inner circles?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: As regards informal meetings and that internal side of its work, I can't remember that Mr. Stakic socialised with Mr. Drljaca. He socialised with Mr. Travar and me, but he socialised more with Mr. Arsic, Simo, and especially with Mr. Kovacevic, because they used to work together at the hospital. Whereas I had no prior contacts, nothing in common with Dr. Stakic before. Regarding this period you are talking about, we only had working contacts about meetings and agreements. Outside of that, I did not meet with Mr. Stakic, with Mr. Simo or the people from the army because our job did not require us to meet in the afternoons or in any nonworking way. I spent my time in the centre for alerting, collecting, and processing information, and I spent most of my time working with Mr. Travar. However, I do not deny that Mr. Stakic spent a lot more time with those other people than with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please have a short glance on S174, then be followed by S72 that we can conclude this line today. Please, always the signature. - 1B, S74-1B. You can identify the paraph one can see there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: No, I can't identify this. I'm completely at a loss about signatures. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So you mentioned previously that you were able to identify with a certain degree of likelihood the signature as it was under the law necessary of Mr. Savanovic. May we please have a look on S80, 8-0. This seems not to be the signature of Dr. Stakic, but can you identify the signature as such? You can see the "za."

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, and I have already told you that I spent time with Mr. Travar, both at work and outside work. And we were close and we had similar viewpoints. I believe that this is the signature of Mr. Travar. It is also quite special, with a little curve on top. And it's as close as I can come to being certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And then S74, please. Whose signature would this be?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: From what I see here, it seems there is a DR. You can conclude from this perhaps that this is Kovacevic's signature because I said before, I didn't often contact this person, and I can't remember his signature precisely. But I believe his signature is a bit longer than the one I'm looking at now. That, at least, is my feeling. I can't confirm one way or another. It is not remarkable in any way. I'm much more certain with regard to the other two persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And then finally for today, because we have to conclude now, S81. Do you recognise this signature? If please the B/C/S version, in this case, could be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR
utterances.text: I can't identify the signature. If you want me to draw conclusions, Bosko associates in my mind with Dr. Mandic. But I'm not at all certain of this. And I didn't see his signature very often, nor did I spend time with this man. I can't be sure. But I don't know any other Bosko than Mandic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clear answer. Then this concludes today's testimony. I kindly have to ask you not to contact any of the parties during the afternoon, evening, and night. One has to be quite concrete. This would be counsel of Prosecution or counsel of Defence, and not discuss with any person you by chance would meet here in The Hague, be it in the hotel or elsewhere, and discuss issues related to your testimony. This concludes today's hearing. We are looking forward to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just ask one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to know the procedure for tomorrow and the day after tomorrow, what am I supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I hope that the line of questions by the Judges can be concluded after the first period of time. This is the first 90 minutes. And then it would be for the parties to put additional questions to you. I don't know. I can't foresee what period of time this will take. So I can't exclude definitely that it might be your testimony will only be concluded Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The trial stays adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: at 1.56 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 4th day of March, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.
